title: Technical Assurance Quick Reference - SIEM & RBAC Evidence Map
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, technical-first reference to speed answers to customer security questionnaires and technical audits that touch on RBAC v2, audit-log schema, SIEM exports, and our evidence automation pipeline. Intended for solutions engineers, security reviewers, and customer success when assembling a short evidence package (15–45 minutes prep).

Scope and audience:
- Focus: what artifacts customers commonly ask for, where to get them, and the minimal context needed for an auditor.
- Audience: SEs, CSMs, security reviewers, partner security teams.
- Not a canonical policy; links to canonical policy and compliance artifacts are below.

Quick evidence map (one-line view):
- Role catalog snapshot: roles.csv (generated from auth-service /roles daily export). Contains role_id, name, description, entitlements, created_by, created_at.
- Role change history: auth-audit.role_changes (append-only), includes before/after diffs, changed_by, ticket_id.
- Access grant events: auth-audit.grants (grant/revoke), includes principal_type (user/service), principal_id, role_id, source (ui/api/sso), request_id.
- Approval artifacts: IAM ticket links (JIRA keys) and signed approval blob when required (approval_signatures bucket).
- Provisioning logs: identity-provisioner logs (OIDC/SCIM syncs) for external directory syncs.
- Administrative actions and policy changes: policy-service.audit (policy_id, change_payload, changed_by).
- Audit log ingestion for SIEM: rlog-v2 JSON lines with schema described below.
- Evidence package: automatic bundler produces a signed tar containing sanitized logs, role snapshots, and a CSV of correlated events.

RBAC v2 - essential artifacts to include for customer review:
- roles.csv export (fields: role_id, stable_name, display_name, description, entitlements[], created_by, last_modified_at)
- role-definition-checksum.txt (SHA256 of canonical role catalog at time of export)
- role_change_history.csv (event_time, event_type, actor, before, after, ticket_id)
- access_events.csv (timestamp, actor, action, resource, role_applied, source_ip, request_id)
- periodic-access-review.pdf (if available) or access-review-logs.csv (review_id, reviewer, decisions)
- proof of least privilege policy doc link (Confluence) and link to policy-service PRs for last 6 months

Lightweight answers for common questionnaire items (copy-and-paste friendly):
Q: How do you manage administrative privileges?
A: Administrative privileges are managed through RBAC v2. Administrators are assigned explicit roles (catalog snapshot attached). Role changes require a documented approval workflow (JIRA tickets) and are captured in the role_change_history audit stream; periodic access reviews are performed quarterly. (See attached role_change_history.csv and approvals folder.)

Q: Do you export audit logs to customer SIEMs?
A: We provide structured, near-real-time audit log exports via secure delivery channels (S3 or customer-managed forwarders). Logs follow our rlog-v2 JSON schema (excerpt below). Delivery can be push (HTTPS webhook/forwarder) or pull (signed S3 export bundles).

Audit log schema (rlog-v2) — minimal, important fields (fields are lower-case):
- event_id: string (UUIDv4)
- timestamp: ISO8601 (UTC)
- service: string (e.g., auth-service, model-router)
- event_type: string (role_change, grant, revoke, login, token_create, api_call)
- actor_type: string (user, service, system)
- actor_id: string (internal id or subject claim for OIDC)
- target_type: string (role, resource, model)
- target_id: string
- outcome: string (success, failure)
- request_id: string (trace id correlated across systems)
- src_ip: string (optional)
- user_agent: string (optional)
- metadata: object (freeform key-values; in exports this is flattened to metadata_key=metadata_value pairs)
- signature: base64 (when exported in signed bundles)

Notes on schema and practical guidance:
- We intentionally keep request_id consistent across components to support event correlation in SIEM.
- metadata is flattened prior to export to avoid nested JSON issues in some SIEMs; keys are prefixed with service name when ambiguous.
- Timestamps are always in UTC and ISO8601.

SIEM export modes and sample filters (operational):
1) Real-time forwarder: JSON lines to customer forwarder endpoint. Recommend Splunk HTTP Event Collector or Sumo Logic endpoint.
2) Batch bundle: daily signed tar.gz stored to customer s3 prefix (encrypted, KMS). Contains rlog-v2/*.jsonl, roles.csv, checksums.
3) Syslog bridge: for legacy environments we can stream key audit events to a syslog aggregator.

Suggested Splunk queries (starter):
- Role change events in last 7d:
  index=redwood sourcetype=rlog event_type=role_change | table timestamp actor_id event_type target_id metadata_ticket_id
- Failed admin actions:
  index=redwood sourcetype=rlog outcome=failure target_type=role OR event_type=grant | stats count by actor_id, target_id, error_code

Evidence automation pipeline (how to reproduce an evidence bundle):
- Trigger: SE requests via internal tool or /evidence-api with a request-id.
- Collection: orchestrator queries auth-service, policy-service, identity-provisioner, and pulls rlog-v2 for the requested time window.
- Sanitize: strip PII, mask IPs (unless customer explicitly requests raw logs), redact prompt/model content per policy.
- Package: generate roles.csv, role_change_history.csv, access_events.csv, checksums, and a signed manifest.
- Delivery: upload to secure staging S3 or push to customer endpoint.
- Audit: bundler emits a delivery_event with request_id and signature recorded in the evidence-trail index.

Operational notes and gotchas (working notes):
- We keep 90 days of hot rlog-v2 in the primary index and archive 1y in cold storage by default; per-customer retention adjustments are under contracts.
- Some older services still emit legacy rlog-v1 events; the bundler normalizes them to rlog-v2 fields but flags anything it could not map.
- When customers request raw prompts or model inputs, consult Legal/Privacy and AE before fulfilling; default is redaction unless GDRP-complete data processing agreement exists.

Templates and quick artifacts to attach (checklist for SE/CSM):
- roles.csv (fresh export)
- role_change_history.csv (last 90 days)
- sample rlog-v2 export (24h window) + checksums
- signed-manifest.txt (SHA256) and delivery_event.json
- pointer to access-review artifacts (PDF or CSV)

Unresolved items / follow-ups (todo):

- Add runbook for emergency evidence requests (24h SLA) and contact matrix (owner: Jonah).
- Decide default IP treatment for evidence bundles (mask or preserve) depending on region (owner: Marco).

Where to find canonical policy and deeper references:
- Confluence: /display/SEC/Operational+Audit+Log+Policy (canonical retention and masking rules)
- Confluence: /display/SEC/Incident+Response+and+Evidence+Handling
- GitHub: repo infra/audit-bundler (implementation of bundler and normalization)
- JIRA: JIRA-SEC-921 (RBAC v2 rollout), JIRA-OPS-1184 (evidence automation staging)

Appendix: short example rlog-v2 JSON line (single line, compact):
{"event_id":"b6f9c2e8-1f1d-4a5f-9c7d-3a5b6d8e4c2a","timestamp":"2026-02-27T18:34:12.345Z","service":"auth-service","event_type":"grant","actor_type":"user","actor_id":"u_12873","target_type":"role","target_id":"role_admin_1","outcome":"success","request_id":"req-0a1b2c3d","src_ip":"203.0.113.12","user_agent":"web-ui/1.4.2","metadata_ticket_id":"JIRA-SEC-734","signature":"BASE64SIG=="}

Notes-to-self style: prioritize making short answer snippets that legal and sales can copy into responses — customers appreciate a 2–3 sentence answer plus attached artifacts. This doc aims to be that.

End of quick reference.
